criteria.criterion: A new test in reading.rs reads a root-cause request that cites two past jobs' introspections as evidence, with no previous_job and no follow-up wording. The reading does not restate those jobs' results and is accepted. Run `cargo test -p athena-core reading`.
criteria.evidence: Ran it: `a_root_cause_request_citing_past_jobs_as_evidence_is_accepted ... ok` (55 passed). The test cites EVIDENCE_A and EVIDENCE_B as introspections, passes attempt=None, and asserts that `followed_up_ids` and `continued_jobs` are empty. The reading names neither job and states no scope, yet `check_reading` accepts it. The test also shows that checking both jobs directly fails with 'the previous result', which is the old behavior.

criteria.criterion: A new test shows that a retry whose reading omits the previous attempt's job id and result is still refused with 'the previous result'. A second test shows that the same retry with a reading that names the previous job is accepted. Run `cargo test -p athena-core reading`.
criteria.evidence: Ran it: `a_retry_whose_reading_omits_the_previous_result_is_refused ... ok` asserts the error contains 'the previous result' and PRIOR_JOB. `a_retry_whose_reading_names_the_previous_job_is_accepted ... ok` passes the same retry with a reading that names PRIOR_JOB. `a_retry_is_checked_even_when_the_request_also_cites_evidence ... ok` also passed.

criteria.criterion: A test shows that a request saying it follows up a named job is checked for that job only. A reading that omits the followed-up job is refused. A different job cited in the same request as evidence is not required to be named.
criteria.evidence: Ran it: `a_follow_up_request_is_checked_for_the_followed_job_only ... ok`. With the request 'This follows up job PRIOR_JOB. Evidence: EVIDENCE_A ...', `continued_jobs` holds only PRIOR_JOB. A reading that omits it is refused, and the error names PRIOR_JOB but not EVIDENCE_A. A reading that names only PRIOR_JOB is accepted. `follow_up_wording_is_matched_narrowly ... ok` covers which phrasings count.

criteria.criterion: read_for passes check_prior_result_and_scope only the retried job and the explicitly followed-up jobs. Evidence-only referenced jobs are still given to the reader in the brief. The doc comments describe this distinction.
criteria.evidence: From reading the code: reading.rs:397 now reads `let priors = continued_jobs(&request.text, attempt, &referenced_jobs);`. `continued_jobs` chains the attempt with the referenced jobs whose id is in `followed_up_ids`. `referenced_jobs` (line 289) is still built from every cited id and put in the brief (line 298). The doc comments on `followed_up_ids`, `continued_jobs`, `referenced_jobs` and `check_prior_result_and_scope` describe the continued-versus-evidence distinction.

criteria.criterion: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` all pass, including the existing prior-result tests.
criteria.evidence: These are Athena's recorded checks on this tree: fmt passed, clippy passed, and `cargo test --locked` passed (1486 tests). criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing that the previous-result check applies only to the continued job and no longer refuses evidence citations.

findings.summary: The new tests check a copy of read_for's logic, not read_for itself
findings.evidence: `check_reading` calls `continued_jobs` and then `check_prior_result_and_scope`, repeating line 397. If line 397 went back to `attempt.into_iter().chain(referenced_jobs.iter())`, every new test would still pass. The real wiring is correct by inspection. A test that runs read_for with a fake reader, or one that uses `hestia::root_cause_request` text, would close the gap.
findings.location: crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs (tests: check_reading helper; read_for at line 397)

findings.summary: No test covers carrying followed-up jobs first
findings.evidence: `referenced_jobs` now puts `followed_up_ids` before the other cited ids so that MAX_REFERENCED_JOBS never drops a followed-up job. No new test sets up more cited jobs than the limit to show this.

findings.summary: A doc-comment line is far longer than the lines around it
findings.evidence: The line '/// that cites jobs as evidence) every reading passes, and so does one that declines the request or asks a question, which has no change to' is well over the roughly 110-character width of the neighbouring comments. rustfmt does not rewrap comments, so the recorded fmt check passed anyway.

summary: The change fixes the problem where it starts. `read_for` used to check every job id cited in the request text. It now passes `check_prior_result_and_scope` only `continued_jobs(...)`: the retried job plus any job the request says it follows up, found by a small, documented phrase match in `followed_up_ids`. Evidence jobs are still carried into the reader's brief with their results. Followed-up jobs are now carried first, so the limit on carried jobs never drops one. I read the change and ran `cargo test -p athena-core reading`: 55 tests passed, including the 6 new ones and the existing prior-result tests. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test runs passed. Only the two expected files changed, and the CHANGELOG entry names the root cause. One weakness: the new tests call a helper that copies `read_for`'s logic instead of calling `read_for` itself. If that one line in `read_for` were reverted, no test would fail. The real wiring at reading.rs:397 is correct by inspection. Other minor points: the follow-up-first ordering of carried jobs has no test, and one doc-comment line is very long. None of these blocks the change.
